mia: Short repro: generator stream stalls when auth refresh runs using the request ctx and the client cancels.
mia: Steps: start stream with ctx timeout, token rotates mid-stream, refresh uses same ctx -> refresh aborts and reconnect loop deadlocks.
raj: Sounds like ctx bleed. Can you paste the minimal pattern?
mia: Simplified anti-pattern: `go refreshToken(ctx)` and `runGenerator(ctx)` where ctx is the request ctx.
tomas: Fix is to separate lifecycles: use request ctx only for the handshake; spawn `streamCtx := context.WithCancel(context.Background())` for background refresh/reconnect and use transient ctxs for each refresh call.
tomas: Example pattern: `rctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second); refresh(rctx); cancel()` inside the background loop. Wire `streamCtx` cancel to stream.Close().
raj: Also gate reconnects with a single worker/mutex so concurrent reconnects don't race. Add a tokenSource abstraction so tests can simulate slow refreshes.
ci-bot: integration (repro-stream-deadlock) failed: TestStreamCancellation flaky; goroutine dump attached.
devex-bot: please open an issue with repro and attach the goroutine dump (link to generator ergonomics template).
mia: I'll file the GH issue and add a tiny failing test + sample app showing the correct `streamCtx` pattern. Thanks for the guidance!
